---
title: "Tensor Regression Simulation Results"
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Tensor Regression Simulation Results}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::knitr}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.align = "center",
  fig.retina = 2
)

data_candidates <- c(
  file.path("inst", "extdata", "rebuttal_tensor_regression"),
  file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", "rebuttal_tensor_regression"),
  system.file(
    "extdata", "rebuttal_tensor_regression", package = "SegreCP"
  )
)
data_candidates <- data_candidates[nzchar(data_candidates)]
existing_candidates <- data_candidates[dir.exists(data_candidates)]
if (!length(existing_candidates)) {
  stop("Cannot locate the frozen rebuttal tensor-regression data.")
}
data_dir <- normalizePath(existing_candidates[[1L]], mustWork = TRUE)

read_rebuttal_csv <- function(filename) {
  path <- file.path(data_dir, filename)
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing frozen artifact: ", filename)
  utils::read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
}

settings <- read_rebuttal_csv("final_settings.csv")
recorded_checks <- read_rebuttal_csv("final_validation_checks.csv")
source_manifest <- read_rebuttal_csv("final_source_artifact_sha256.csv")
checkpoint_manifest <- read_rebuttal_csv("checkpoint_source_manifest.csv")
grid_raw <- read_rebuttal_csv("final_seven_method_grid_raw.csv")
checkpoint_raw <- read_rebuttal_csv("checkpoint_metrics_raw.csv")
timing_raw <- read_rebuttal_csv(
  "final_seven_method_serial_timing_raw.csv"
)

method_order <- c(
  "CP-ALS", "RRR", "Tucker-RGD", "HOPLS", "TT-IHT", "RGD", "RGN"
)
checkpoint_methods <- setdiff(method_order, "HOPLS")
iterative_methods <- setdiff(method_order, "HOPLS")

method_colors <- c(
  "CP-ALS" = "#303030",
  "RRR" = "#858585",
  "Tucker-RGD" = "#686868",
  "HOPLS" = "#A3A3A3",
  "TT-IHT" = "#B5B5B5",
  "RGD" = "#D55E00",
  "RGN" = "#0072B2"
)
method_points <- c(
  "CP-ALS" = 15,
  "RRR" = 1,
  "Tucker-RGD" = 0,
  "HOPLS" = 5,
  "TT-IHT" = 2,
  "RGD" = 17,
  "RGN" = 16
)
method_lines <- c(
  "CP-ALS" = 3,
  "RRR" = 4,
  "Tucker-RGD" = 5,
  "HOPLS" = 6,
  "TT-IHT" = 6,
  "RGD" = 2,
  "RGN" = 1
)

metric_columns <- c(
  "coefficient_error", "train_rmse", "test_rmse",
  "clean_test_rmse", "relative_prediction_error"
)

# Balance the 12 coherence/noise cells within each replication before taking
# a mean and Monte Carlo standard error across replications. This is the
# aggregation used for the rebuttal's across-grid panel.
replication_balanced <- stats::aggregate(
  grid_raw[metric_columns],
  grid_raw[c("display_method", "replication")],
  mean
)
accuracy_mean <- stats::aggregate(
  replication_balanced[metric_columns],
  replication_balanced["display_method"],
  mean
)
accuracy_se <- stats::aggregate(
  replication_balanced[metric_columns],
  replication_balanced["display_method"],
  function(x) stats::sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))
)
names(accuracy_se)[-1L] <- paste0(names(accuracy_se)[-1L], "_se")
accuracy_summary <- merge(
  accuracy_mean, accuracy_se, by = "display_method", sort = FALSE
)
accuracy_summary <- accuracy_summary[
  match(method_order, accuracy_summary$display_method),
]

checkpoint_mean <- stats::aggregate(
  checkpoint_raw["coefficient_error"],
  checkpoint_raw[c("method", "iteration")],
  mean
)
checkpoint_se <- stats::aggregate(
  checkpoint_raw["coefficient_error"],
  checkpoint_raw[c("method", "iteration")],
  function(x) stats::sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))
)
names(checkpoint_mean)[3L] <- "error_mean"
names(checkpoint_se)[3L] <- "error_se"
checkpoint_summary <- merge(
  checkpoint_mean, checkpoint_se,
  by = c("method", "iteration"), sort = FALSE
)
checkpoint_summary$ci_lower <- NA_real_
checkpoint_summary$ci_upper <- NA_real_
for (row_id in seq_len(nrow(checkpoint_summary))) {
  row <- checkpoint_summary[row_id, ]
  values <- checkpoint_raw$coefficient_error[
    checkpoint_raw$method == row$method &
      checkpoint_raw$iteration == row$iteration
  ]
  set.seed(20260829L + 800000L + row_id)
  bootstrap_means <- replicate(
    2000L,
    mean(sample(values, size = length(values), replace = TRUE))
  )
  checkpoint_summary$ci_lower[[row_id]] <- stats::quantile(
    bootstrap_means, 0.025, names = FALSE, type = 8
  )
  checkpoint_summary$ci_upper[[row_id]] <- stats::quantile(
    bootstrap_means, 0.975, names = FALSE, type = 8
  )
}

high_raw <- grid_raw[grid_raw$coherence == 0.75, ]
high_mean <- stats::aggregate(
  high_raw["clean_test_rmse"],
  high_raw[c("display_method", "noise_sd")],
  mean
)
high_se <- stats::aggregate(
  high_raw["clean_test_rmse"],
  high_raw[c("display_method", "noise_sd")],
  function(x) stats::sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))
)
names(high_mean)[3L] <- "rmse_mean"
names(high_se)[3L] <- "rmse_se"
high_summary <- merge(
  high_mean, high_se,
  by = c("display_method", "noise_sd"), sort = FALSE
)

timing_mean <- stats::aggregate(
  timing_raw["reported_fit_sec"], timing_raw["display_method"], mean
)
timing_se <- stats::aggregate(
  timing_raw["reported_fit_sec"], timing_raw["display_method"],
  function(x) stats::sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))
)
names(timing_mean)[2L] <- "time_mean"
names(timing_se)[2L] <- "time_se"
timing_summary <- merge(
  timing_mean, timing_se, by = "display_method", sort = FALSE
)
timing_summary <- timing_summary[
  match(method_order, timing_summary$display_method),
]

summary_with_time <- merge(
  accuracy_summary, timing_summary, by = "display_method", sort = FALSE
)
summary_with_time <- summary_with_time[
  match(method_order, summary_with_time$display_method),
]

grid_pair_counts <- table(
  grid_raw$coherence, grid_raw$noise_sd, grid_raw$replication
)
grid_seed_counts <- stats::aggregate(
  grid_raw["seed"],
  grid_raw[c("coherence", "noise_sd", "replication")],
  function(x) length(unique(x))
)
checkpoint_counts <- table(
  checkpoint_raw$method, checkpoint_raw$iteration
)
checkpoint_winners <- vapply(c(3, 5, 10), function(iteration) {
  z <- checkpoint_summary[checkpoint_summary$iteration == iteration, ]
  z$method[[which.min(z$error_mean)]]
}, character(1L))
checkpoint_means_decrease <- all(vapply(
  split(checkpoint_summary, checkpoint_summary$method),
  function(z) {
    z <- z[order(z$iteration), ]
    all(diff(z$error_mean) < 0)
  },
  logical(1L)
))
high_rank_is_reproduced <- all(vapply(c(0, 0.5, 1), function(noise) {
  z <- high_summary[high_summary$noise_sd == noise, ]
  ranked <- z$display_method[order(z$rmse_mean)]
  if (noise == 0) {
    identical(ranked[[1L]], "Tucker-RGD")
  } else {
    setequal(ranked[1:2], c("RGD", "RGN"))
  }
}, logical(1L)))
accuracy_pair_is_reproduced <-
  setequal(
    accuracy_summary$display_method[
      order(accuracy_summary$coefficient_error)[1:2]
    ],
    c("RGD", "RGN")
  ) &&
  setequal(
    accuracy_summary$display_method[
      order(accuracy_summary$clean_test_rmse)[1:2]
    ],
    c("RGD", "RGN")
  )

recomputed_checks <- data.frame(
  check = c(
    "1,680 paired grid rows",
    "exact seven-method set",
    "complete 4 x 3 x 20 x 7 grid",
    "one seed per paired cell",
    "finite accuracy metrics",
    "fixed ten-update budget for iterative methods",
    "360 complete checkpoint rows",
    "checkpoint means and winners reproduce Panel A",
    "high-coherence winners reproduce Panel B",
    "RGD/RGN reproduce the across-grid accuracy pair",
    "140 serial timing rows at rho=0.5, sigma=0.5",
    "all recorded source validations passed"
  ),
  passed = c(
    nrow(grid_raw) == 1680L,
    identical(sort(unique(grid_raw$display_method)), sort(method_order)),
    identical(dim(grid_pair_counts), c(4L, 3L, 20L)) &&
      all(grid_pair_counts == 7L),
    all(grid_seed_counts$seed == 1L),
    all(vapply(grid_raw[metric_columns], function(x) all(is.finite(x)),
               logical(1L))),
    all(grid_raw$attempted_iterations[
      grid_raw$display_method %in% iterative_methods
    ] == 10L) &&
      all(grid_raw$accepted_iterations[
        grid_raw$display_method %in% iterative_methods
      ] == 10L),
    nrow(checkpoint_raw) == 360L &&
      identical(sort(unique(checkpoint_raw$method)),
                sort(checkpoint_methods)) &&
      all(checkpoint_counts == 20L),
    checkpoint_means_decrease &&
      identical(checkpoint_winners, c("RGN", "RGN", "CP-ALS")),
    high_rank_is_reproduced,
    accuracy_pair_is_reproduced,
    nrow(timing_raw) == 140L &&
      all(timing_raw$coherence == 0.5) &&
      all(timing_raw$noise_sd == 0.5) &&
      all(table(timing_raw$display_method) == 20L),
    all(recorded_checks$passed)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

runtime <- stats::setNames(
  timing_summary$time_mean, timing_summary$display_method
)
runtime_tier_order_holds <-
  max(runtime[c("RGD", "RGN")]) < runtime[["CP-ALS"]] &&
  runtime[["CP-ALS"]] < runtime[["HOPLS"]] &&
  runtime[["HOPLS"]] < runtime[["TT-IHT"]] &&
  runtime[["TT-IHT"]] < min(runtime[c("RRR", "Tucker-RGD")])

stopifnot(all(recomputed_checks$passed), runtime_tier_order_holds)
```

## Scope

This vignette reproduces the synthetic tensor-on-tensor regression experiment
that was reported as a three-panel table during the rebuttal. It does **not**
use the design, output, or plotting data behind the manuscript's former
Figure 1. The figures below are computed from the frozen replicate-level
records shipped in `inst/extdata/rebuttal_tensor_regression`.

The competing-method rows are frozen numerical evidence, not installed
estimators. `SegreCP` exposes only RGD, RGN, and their initialization layer; the
current comparator entry point is maintained outside the built package.

We use *reproduce* in a specific sense here: all displayed summaries are
recomputed from the paired raw records, rather than copied from the formatted
rebuttal table. The source manifest records the full simulation runner that
generated those records; the vignette itself does not rerun the full benchmark
during package building.

## Frozen design and implementations

```{r settings-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  settings,
  col.names = c("Design item", "Frozen value"),
  align = c("l", "l")
)
```

The coefficient tensor has two output modes and three predictor modes, all of
dimension 10. Within each coherence/replication pair, the methods use the same
coefficient tensor, training and test designs, and standardized noise arrays;
only the noise multiplier changes across the three noise levels. CP-ALS, RGD,
and RGN also share the same computed CPCA object. RRR, Tucker-RGD, HOPLS, and
TT-IHT use the native parameterizations and initializations specified in the
rebuttal experiment. HOPLS extracts three latent blocks, so it has no entry in
an outer-iteration checkpoint comparison.

## Integrity checks before plotting

```{r integrity-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  recomputed_checks,
  col.names = c("Check recomputed in this vignette", "Passed"),
  align = c("l", "c")
)
```

All `r nrow(recomputed_checks)` checks pass. The accompanying source manifest
contains `r nrow(source_manifest)` SHA-256 records for the frozen runner,
solver sources, source result files, validation files, seed schedules, data
fingerprints, and session records. A separate `r nrow(checkpoint_manifest)`-row
manifest records the inputs and derived hash for the checkpoint archive. The
checkpoint artifact is dedicated to
the rebuttal's noiseless `rho = 0.5` setting; those two design values are
file-level metadata rather than repeated columns in that compact CSV.

## Noiseless optimization checkpoints

The first rebuttal panel recorded relative coefficient error after 3, 5, and
10 outer updates at `(rho, sigma) = (0.5, 0)`. These are three deliberately
recorded checkpoints, not a measurement at every intermediate update.

```{r checkpoint-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8.6, fig.height=5.6, fig.cap="Noiseless optimization checkpoints. Points are means over 20 paired replications; bars are deterministic 95% percentile-bootstrap intervals for the mean. The y axis is logarithmic."}
plot_checkpoint_figure <- function() {
  old_par <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(graphics::par(old_par))
  graphics::par(mar = c(7.4, 5.2, 3.5, 1.4), xpd = FALSE)

  lower <- checkpoint_summary$ci_lower
  upper <- checkpoint_summary$ci_upper
  y_limits <- range(c(lower, upper)) * c(0.7, 1.4)

  graphics::plot(
    NA_real_, NA_real_,
    xlim = c(2.6, 10.4), ylim = y_limits, log = "y",
    xaxt = "n", xlab = "Recorded outer-update checkpoint",
    ylab = "Relative coefficient error",
    main = "Noiseless optimization checkpoints"
  )
  graphics::axis(1, at = c(3, 5, 10))
  graphics::abline(
    h = 10^seq(floor(log10(y_limits[[1L]])),
               ceiling(log10(y_limits[[2L]]))),
    col = "#E8E8E8", lwd = 0.8
  )
  graphics::mtext(
    "rho = 0.5; sigma = 0; 20 paired replications",
    side = 3, line = 0.45, cex = 0.82, col = "#4A4A4A"
  )

  draw_order <- c("RRR", "TT-IHT", "Tucker-RGD", "CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")
  for (method in draw_order) {
    z <- checkpoint_summary[checkpoint_summary$method == method, ]
    z <- z[order(z$iteration), ]
    lo <- z$ci_lower
    hi <- z$ci_upper
    graphics::segments(
      z$iteration, lo, z$iteration, hi,
      col = method_colors[[method]], lwd = 1
    )
    graphics::segments(
      z$iteration - 0.07, lo, z$iteration + 0.07, lo,
      col = method_colors[[method]], lwd = 1
    )
    graphics::segments(
      z$iteration - 0.07, hi, z$iteration + 0.07, hi,
      col = method_colors[[method]], lwd = 1
    )
    graphics::lines(
      z$iteration, z$error_mean,
      col = method_colors[[method]], lty = method_lines[[method]],
      lwd = if (method %in% c("RGD", "RGN")) 2.1 else 1.35
    )
    graphics::points(
      z$iteration, z$error_mean,
      col = method_colors[[method]], pch = method_points[[method]],
      cex = if (method %in% c("RGD", "RGN")) 1.05 else 0.9,
      lwd = 1.2
    )
  }

  graphics::par(xpd = NA)
  legend_order <- c("RGN", "RGD", "CP-ALS", "Tucker-RGD", "TT-IHT", "RRR")
  user_coordinates <- graphics::par("usr")
  legend_y <- 10^(
    user_coordinates[[3L]] -
      0.25 * (user_coordinates[[4L]] - user_coordinates[[3L]])
  )
  graphics::legend(
    x = mean(c(2.6, 10.4)), y = legend_y,
    xjust = 0.5, yjust = 1, horiz = TRUE,
    legend = legend_order,
    col = method_colors[legend_order], pch = method_points[legend_order],
    lty = method_lines[legend_order],
    lwd = c(2.1, 2.1, rep(1.35, 4)),
    pt.cex = 0.85, cex = 0.72, bty = "n"
  )
}

plot_checkpoint_figure()
```

At the recorded checkpoints, RGN has the smallest mean error at iterations 3
and 5; CP-ALS is marginally smaller at iteration 10. Every displayed group
mean decreases over the three checkpoints. The connected segments are visual
guides between separately recorded fits. This is an empirical optimization
diagnostic for the frozen noiseless design, not a proof of global convergence
or of per-replication monotonicity at unobserved updates.

## High-coherence stress setting

The second rebuttal panel fixed `rho = 0.75` and compared terminal clean-test
RMSE across the three noise levels. Clean-test RMSE removes newly generated
test noise from the target, so it directly measures recovery of the predictive
signal in this synthetic experiment.

```{r high-coherence-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=11.2, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap="High-coherence clean-test RMSE. Points are means over 20 paired replications; horizontal bars are mean plus or minus 1.96 Monte Carlo standard errors. All panels share a logarithmic x scale."}
plot_high_coherence_figure <- function() {
  old_par <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(graphics::par(old_par))
  graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 3), oma = c(3.2, 0, 3.2, 0))

  lower <- pmax(
    high_summary$rmse_mean - 1.96 * high_summary$rmse_se,
    .Machine$double.xmin
  )
  upper <- high_summary$rmse_mean + 1.96 * high_summary$rmse_se
  x_limits <- range(c(lower, upper)) * c(0.75, 1.3)
  display_order <- method_order
  y_position <- rev(seq_along(display_order))
  names(y_position) <- display_order

  for (panel in seq_along(c(0, 0.5, 1))) {
    noise <- c(0, 0.5, 1)[[panel]]
    z <- high_summary[high_summary$noise_sd == noise, ]
    z <- z[match(display_order, z$display_method), ]
    graphics::par(mar = c(3.9, if (panel == 1L) 7.2 else 1.1, 2.4, 1.0))
    graphics::plot(
      NA_real_, NA_real_,
      xlim = x_limits, ylim = c(0.5, length(display_order) + 0.5),
      log = "x", yaxt = "n", ylab = "", xlab = "",
      main = paste0("sigma = ", format(noise, trim = TRUE))
    )
    if (panel == 1L) {
      graphics::axis(
        2, at = y_position, labels = display_order,
        las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.78
      )
    }
    graphics::abline(v = 10^(-6:-2), col = "#ECECEC", lwd = 0.8)
    lo <- pmax(z$rmse_mean - 1.96 * z$rmse_se,
               .Machine$double.xmin)
    hi <- z$rmse_mean + 1.96 * z$rmse_se
    y <- unname(y_position[z$display_method])
    graphics::segments(lo, y, hi, y,
                       col = method_colors[z$display_method], lwd = 1.2)
    graphics::segments(lo, y - 0.08, lo, y + 0.08,
                       col = method_colors[z$display_method], lwd = 1)
    graphics::segments(hi, y - 0.08, hi, y + 0.08,
                       col = method_colors[z$display_method], lwd = 1)
    graphics::points(
      z$rmse_mean, y,
      col = method_colors[z$display_method],
      pch = method_points[z$display_method], cex = 0.95, lwd = 1.2
    )
  }

  graphics::mtext(
    "High-coherence clean-test RMSE",
    side = 3, outer = TRUE, line = 1.55, cex = 1.05, font = 2
  )
  graphics::mtext(
    "rho = 0.75; 20 paired replications per noise level",
    side = 3, outer = TRUE, line = 0.3, cex = 0.82, col = "#4A4A4A"
  )
  graphics::mtext(
    "Clean-test RMSE (log scale)",
    side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 1.45, cex = 0.88
  )
}

plot_high_coherence_figure()
```

The best method changes with the regime. Tucker-RGD has the smallest mean
clean-test RMSE in the noiseless high-coherence cell. At `sigma = 0.5` and
`sigma = 1`, RGD and RGN are the lowest two means, with CP-ALS close behind.
This pattern is more informative than a claim of uniform dominance.

## Across-grid accuracy and reference-machine time

The third rebuttal panel first averaged each metric equally over all 12
coherence/noise cells within a replication, then averaged the 20 resulting
replication-level values. The table below is rebuilt from the raw grid and
serial timing records.

```{r reproduced-table, echo=FALSE}
reproduced_table <- data.frame(
  Method = summary_with_time$display_method,
  `Coefficient error` = formatC(
    summary_with_time$coefficient_error, format = "e", digits = 4
  ),
  `Clean RMSE` = formatC(
    summary_with_time$clean_test_rmse, format = "e", digits = 5
  ),
  `Noisy RMSE` = formatC(
    summary_with_time$test_rmse, format = "e", digits = 5
  ),
  `Reference time (s)` = formatC(
    summary_with_time$time_mean, format = "f", digits = 3
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(reproduced_table, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

```{r tradeoff-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10.2, fig.height=5.1, fig.cap="Cell-balanced accuracy and reference-machine fit time. Accuracy means and standard errors are computed across 20 replication-balanced summaries; time means and standard errors use 20 serial fits at rho = 0.5 and sigma = 0.5. The time axis is logarithmic."}
plot_tradeoff_figure <- function() {
  old_par <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(graphics::par(old_par))
  graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 2), oma = c(3.3, 0, 3.5, 0))

  label_position <- c(
    "CP-ALS" = 4, "RRR" = 3, "Tucker-RGD" = 4,
    "HOPLS" = 2, "TT-IHT" = 2, "RGD" = 4, "RGN" = 2
  )
  panels <- list(
    list(
      metric = "coefficient_error", se = "coefficient_error_se",
      label = "Relative coefficient error"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "clean_test_rmse", se = "clean_test_rmse_se",
      label = "Clean-test RMSE"
    )
  )

  for (panel in panels) {
    y <- summary_with_time[[panel$metric]]
    y_se <- summary_with_time[[panel$se]]
    y_lo <- pmax(y - 1.96 * y_se, 0)
    y_hi <- y + 1.96 * y_se
    y_padding <- diff(range(c(y_lo, y_hi))) * 0.08
    y_limits <- range(c(y_lo, y_hi)) + c(-y_padding, y_padding)
    x <- summary_with_time$time_mean
    x_lo <- pmax(x - 1.96 * summary_with_time$time_se,
                 .Machine$double.xmin)
    x_hi <- x + 1.96 * summary_with_time$time_se

    graphics::par(mar = c(4.0, 5.0, 2.0, 1.2))
    graphics::plot(
      NA_real_, NA_real_, xlim = c(0.075, 7.5), ylim = y_limits,
      log = "x", xlab = "", ylab = panel$label
    )
    graphics::abline(v = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2),
                     col = "#ECECEC", lwd = 0.8)
    graphics::abline(h = pretty(y_limits), col = "#F0F0F0", lwd = 0.8)
    graphics::segments(
      x_lo, y, x_hi, y,
      col = method_colors[summary_with_time$display_method], lwd = 1
    )
    graphics::segments(
      x, y_lo, x, y_hi,
      col = method_colors[summary_with_time$display_method], lwd = 1
    )
    graphics::points(
      x, y,
      col = method_colors[summary_with_time$display_method],
      pch = method_points[summary_with_time$display_method],
      cex = 1.0, lwd = 1.2
    )
    graphics::text(
      x, y, labels = summary_with_time$display_method,
      pos = unname(label_position[summary_with_time$display_method]),
      offset = 0.42, cex = 0.72,
      col = method_colors[summary_with_time$display_method]
    )
  }

  graphics::mtext(
    "Cell-balanced accuracy and reference-machine fit time",
    side = 3, outer = TRUE, line = 1.75, cex = 1.05, font = 2
  )
  graphics::mtext(
    "Lower and further left is better; means plus or minus 1.96 Monte Carlo standard errors",
    side = 3, outer = TRUE, line = 0.45, cex = 0.8, col = "#4A4A4A"
  )
  graphics::mtext(
    "Mean fit time in seconds on the reference machine (log scale)",
    side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 1.5, cex = 0.88
  )
}

plot_tradeoff_figure()
```

RGD and RGN form the lowest-error pair for both coefficient recovery and
clean prediction, and they occupy the fastest runtime tier in this recorded
experiment. Their accuracy differences are small relative to their
Monte Carlo uncertainty. The noisy-test RMSE is retained in the reconstructed
table because it was reported in the rebuttal, but response noise compresses
the separation between methods.

## Runtime validation uses tiers, not exact seconds

Absolute wall-clock seconds depend on hardware, BLAS, process load, and timer
granularity. The frozen records retain the original seconds for provenance,
but neither those values nor the order within two nearly tied pairs is used as
a package pass/fail threshold. A fresh run is considered consistent with the
rebuttal when it preserves the following well-separated partial order:

```{r runtime-tier-table, echo=FALSE}
runtime_tiers <- data.frame(
  Tier = 1:5,
  Methods = c(
    "RGD and RGN",
    "CP-ALS",
    "HOPLS",
    "TT-IHT",
    "RRR and Tucker-RGD"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  runtime_tiers,
  col.names = c("Runtime tier (fast to slow)", "Methods"),
  align = c("c", "l")
)
```

Thus the portable runtime statement is

\[
\{\mathrm{RGD},\mathrm{RGN}\}
< \mathrm{CP\mbox{-}ALS}
< \mathrm{HOPLS}
< \mathrm{TT\mbox{-}IHT}
< \{\mathrm{RRR},\mathrm{Tucker\mbox{-}RGD}\}.
\]

We do not interpret the within-pair order of RGD versus RGN, or RRR versus
Tucker-RGD, as reproducible evidence.

## What this reproduction supports

The raw-record checks, aggregation reconstruction, and visual diagnostics make
the rebuttal table auditable. In this frozen design they show rapid early
progress by RGN, decreasing mean errors over the recorded noiseless
checkpoints, regime-dependent behavior under high coherence, and a favorable
accuracy--runtime tier for RGD/RGN.

They do not prove global convergence, observe every intermediate update, or
show that one method dominates for every tensor dimension, rank, coherence,
noise level, initialization, or computing environment. Those are deliberately
separate claims from reproducibility of this particular rebuttal experiment.
